candidates.stem: You are managing a seafood distributor's shipment-spoilage classifier, recently deployed using BigQuery ML boosted trees. Training joins dispatch records with completed-trip summaries, including maximum transit temperature and actual journey duration. A random holdout showed strong performance, but dispatch-time predictions are poor. The scoring query supplies missing values for these summaries because they become available after delivery. You want the classifier to learn from features available at dispatch while minimizing changes to the team's BigQuery SQL training and prediction workflow. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Move the existing joined training dataset to Agent Platform AutoML tabular classification, then use automated training to rebuild the shipment-spoilage classifier with those features.

options.label: B
options.text: Increase L1 regularization when retraining the BigQuery ML boosted tree classifier, letting the stronger penalty determine which features from the joined dataset remain useful.

options.label: C
options.text: Rank the existing BigQuery ML features by global feature importance, then retrain the classifier using the highest-ranked features from the joined training dataset.

options.label: D
options.text: Retrain the BigQuery ML classifier using a training query that explicitly selects dispatch-available features and excludes completed-trip summaries from the model inputs.

rationales.A: This fails to correct the training feature selection. Agent Platform AutoML automates tasks such as architecture selection, hyperparameter tuning, and machine provisioning. Supplying the same joined dataset still supplies completed-trip summaries unavailable at dispatch. Selecting the appropriate columns in the existing BigQuery ML training query addresses the issue with fewer workflow changes.
rationales.B: This fails to ensure that training features are available at dispatch. BigQuery ML supports L1 regularization for boosted trees, but changing its amount does not change which columns the training query supplies. The completed-trip summaries remain candidate inputs rather than being excluded according to their availability.
rationales.C: This fails to ensure that selected features are available at dispatch. BigQuery ML global explanations evaluate feature importance to the model. Importance does not establish when a feature becomes available, so selecting highly ranked features can retain the completed-trip summaries.
rationales.D: The goals are to use features available at dispatch and minimize changes to the SQL workflow. BigQuery ML generates training data from the training query, so explicitly selecting dispatch-available features removes the unavailable summaries while preserving the existing workflow. Feature importance and regularization do not select columns according to availability, and moving the unchanged dataset to Agent Platform AutoML leaves the problematic inputs in training.

candidates.stem: Your company uses a support-ticket classifier to route urgent customer requests. Production monitoring shows inconsistent results across nightly releases. An existing scheduler runs custom training jobs, and jobs with identical hyperparameters resume the same run in Agent Platform Experiments. Model Registry stores released versions. You want release comparisons to retain each training execution's parameters, metrics, and model artifacts while minimizing changes to the functioning scheduler and training code. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Log each nightly job's training curves separately in Agent Platform TensorBoard. Compare curves by release date and inspect Model Registry versions as the historical record for monitored releases.

options.label: B
options.text: Use Model Registry versions as the release comparison records. Add the shared Agent Platform Experiments run name to each version's description, then inspect that run for the training parameters, metrics, and artifacts.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a distinct Agent Platform Experiments run for each training execution. Log its parameters and metrics, associate uniquely identified model artifacts, and record the mapping to its Model Registry version.

options.label: D
options.text: Resume the existing Agent Platform Experiments run for each hyperparameter configuration. Attach every nightly model artifact and log the latest metrics there, using this consolidated record to compare registered model releases.

rationales.A: Agent Platform TensorBoard stores time series metrics, which help compare training behavior. Separate curves and Model Registry versions do not, by themselves, record which execution produced each model artifact. This leaves the required release-to-training lineage incomplete. Agent Platform Experiments tracks execution inputs and output artifacts, providing the associations needed for these comparisons.
rationales.B: Model Registry versions distinguish released models and allow version descriptions. However, putting the same experiment-run name in every description still points releases to a combined training record. This fails to preserve independently comparable execution records: creating model versions does not separate the executions already consolidated into one Agent Platform Experiments run.
rationales.C: The goal is to compare release-specific training records and artifacts with minimal workflow changes. Agent Platform Experiments represents each execution as a run and tracks its parameters, metrics, and artifacts. Creating distinct runs and recording their mappings to Model Registry versions preserves those associations within the existing workflow. Shared runs combine execution records, references from Model Registry do not separate them, and training curves alone do not establish artifact lineage.
rationales.D: This fails to preserve independently comparable training executions. Resuming an Agent Platform Experiments run continues the existing run rather than creating a new one. Summary metrics have a single value for each metric key in a run, so attaching successive artifacts to that shared record does not preserve separate execution-level comparisons.
